series.title: Oakhaven Adventures

questGiver.name: Noll Vey
questGiver.why: His apprentice is missing and the bell is ringing on his water. He hires the party at the ferry stair.

series.mayorFrame: Only level 1 and level 10 are the mayor's quests. This module's giver is the NPC in questGiver. Do not move this job onto the mayor's desk.

setup.pitch: The Night Spring soundings end beneath the Mere, where a drowned warning bell has begun ringing underwater and a ferryman's apprentice vanished while investigating it.
setup.openingLocation: Noll Vey's ferry landing on the Mere
setup.gmSummary: The party follows blackwater soundings to the Mere after locals hear a bell ringing beneath still water. Ferryman Noll Vey's apprentice, Tamsin Reed, disappeared while checking the flooded bell-house. The party crosses reed channels, descends through a half-submerged bell-house, and reconstructs a three-note warning sequence from physical inscriptions and drowned keeper records. The apparent haunting is Bellkeeper Ysra, who is not trying to drown intruders; she is repeatedly sounding the old contamination warning because the Night Spring is carrying buried corruption into the Mere. Ringing the proper sequence opens the founder's dry archive chamber, releases Ysra from duty, and reveals that the spring was deliberately diverted from beneath Oakhaven's Founders' Crypt generations ago. Pace: Noll's hire at the stair, a rolled encounter before the chart, the false buoy, a second roll on the crossing, arrival at the bell-house with the water trap and the note puzzle, Ysra holding the warning, the return to the stair, and the Founders' Crypt lead. Pace: Noll's hire at the stair, a rolled encounter before the chart, the false buoy, a second roll on the crossing, arrival at the bell-house with the water trap and the note puzzle, Ysra holding the warning, the return to the stair, and the Founders' Crypt lead.
setup.background: Before Oakhaven built its later wards, the Mere bell-house monitored groundwater and flood channels. Bellkeeper Ysra was ordered to sound three notes if tainted water reached the Mere. During a catastrophic flood, the bell-house sank, Ysra died at her post, and the warning system was abandoned. The Night Spring now carries the same corruption route past the Ashen Bridge into the Mere. Ysra's echo continues the last duty she understood: ring the warning until someone answers correctly.
setup.standaloneStart: If prior Oakhaven modules were not played, Noll Vey hires the party after his apprentice Tamsin disappears near a submerged bell-house that has started ringing beneath calm water.

quest.objective: Find Tamsin Reed, learn why the drowned bell is ringing, and stop the underwater warning without silencing whatever truth it protects.
quest.stakes: Every failed bell attempt raises the Mere inside the ruin. At Mere Level 3, lower chambers become fully submerged and the dry archive can only be reached through the emergency air shaft.
quest.deadline: MERE LEVEL 0–3. Increase by 1 after a wrong bell sequence or a long delay inside the drowned bell-house. Level 3 changes routes but never locks the ending.
successConditions: Tamsin Reed is rescued or her fate is determined.
The three-note warning sequence is understood and resolved.
Bellkeeper Ysra is released or the bell is deliberately silenced after the archive truth is recovered.
failureConditions: The party destroys the bell mechanism before recovering the founder archive and then abandons the site.
The party leaves Tamsin trapped in the bell-house.

facts.text: Bellkeeper Ysra's ghost is sounding an old contamination warning, not trying to lure people to their deaths.
The warning sequence is LOW → HIGH → LOW, representing water below, alarm above, and water withdrawn.
Tamsin is alive in a trapped air pocket below the bell deck.
Oakhaven's founders deliberately diverted the Night Spring away from their crypt and toward the Mere.
The founder archive identifies a sealed relief tunnel back toward the Founders' Crypt under Oakhaven.

secrets.text: Ysra was ordered to keep ringing even after evacuation because town leaders feared panic more than losing the bellkeeper.
secrets.revealCondition: Read the sealed duty order in the archive or earn Ysra's trust after completing the warning sequence.

uses water depth instead of distance
wants: The bell explained before fishermen abandon the Mere

Tamsin took a pry bar, rope, and hooded lantern

revealRules.when: The party asks how she reached the ruin.

npcs.questFunction: Gets the party onto the Mere, makes the missing-person stake personal, and frames the bell as a possible warning rather than an automatic enemy.
npcs.description: A square-built ferryman in a patched oilskin coat, holding one oar under his arm and Tamsin's spare red scarf knotted around his wrist.
tableDialogue: “Bells do not ring underwater unless somebody wants to be heard.”
“Bring Tamsin back. Then we can decide whether the dead get to keep their bell.”
“The water is wrong when it goes quiet. That is when the ringing starts.”

reactions.agreement: Provides a flat-bottomed ferry, three cork floats, and a weighted line.
reactions.refusal: Leaves the ferry tied and tells the party they can borrow it if they change their minds.
reactions.danger: Rows injured survivors back to shore while the party finishes the ruin.
reactions.accusation: Takes responsibility for sending Tamsin alone, but says the ringing had already become dangerous enough that someone had to investigate.

npcs.name: Tamsin Reed
npcs.role: missing ferryman apprentice trapped in an air pocket
wants: Her notes preserved so the trip meant something
fears: Ysra being destroyed before anyone understands her
knows: The bell has two reachable strike points that make low/high tones
The wall inscription uses three water-line symbols
Ysra stopped attacking when Tamsin copied the symbols
believes: The ghost is repeating a warning procedure
secrets: She rang the wrong sequence once and flooded the lower stairs
cannotKnow: What is inside the founder archive

revealRules.fact: LOW and HIGH are produced from different bell strike points.
revealRules.when: The party frees her or speaks through the grate.

revealRules.fact: She already tried HIGH → LOW and caused the flood surge.
revealRules.when: The party asks what she tested.

npcs.questFunction: Provides rescue stakes and practical sound-puzzle knowledge without being the only source of the solution.
npcs.description: A young ferryman wedged into a brick air pocket under the bell deck, soaked to the shoulders, with charcoal symbols copied across one forearm.
tableDialogue: “Do not ring it high first. I learned that one for all of us.”
“The ghost keeps pointing at the water marks, not at me.”
“There are two tones. Three marks. I think the middle note is the alarm.”

reactions.agreement: Hands over her charcoal rubbing and helps strike the sequence once freed.
reactions.refusal: Still passes the rubbing through the grate; she wants the puzzle solved more than credit.
reactions.danger: Uses the air pocket rope to anchor anyone swept off the lower stairs.
reactions.accusation: Admits she rang the wrong sequence and caused the lower flood surge, then immediately shows the rubbing so nobody repeats it.

voiceCues: voice arrives a heartbeat after the bell stops vibrating

fears: The bell being broken before the warning is understood
The founders' diversion being forgotten again
knows: The archive opens after the proper response
The Night Spring was diverted from the Founders' Crypt
believes: Duty ends only when a living witness repeats the warning and opens the archive
secrets: She was ordered to keep ringing after everyone else evacuated

revealRules.when: A character presents the keeper badge or repeats any two correct notes.
The archive opens or the full sequence is rung.

npcs.questFunction: Provides a social alternative to fighting the haunting and turns the bell sequence into an acknowledgment ritual rather than a lock code.
npcs.description: A translucent woman in an old bellkeeper coat, seen only where ripples reflect the bronze bell; water pours endlessly from her sleeves without wetting the floor.

reactions.agreement: Stops creating grasping-water hazards and points toward the archive latch.
reactions.refusal: Continues the warning cycle but never withholds physical clues.
reactions.danger: Defends the bell with waves and pushing water; she avoids lethal harm.
reactions.accusation: Points to the founder duty order rather than arguing; she wants the living to judge the command after they understand what it required.

locations.name: Mere Ferry Landing
locations.description: Gray water stretches beyond reed islands beneath a low sky, and a red scarf hangs from an empty ferry post while no wind disturbs the surface. Tar, wet rope, and fish oil cling to the landing, where the tied ferry is the only practical route into the Mere.

locations.name: The Silent Reeds
locations.description: A narrow channel winds through head-high reeds that scrape the ferry hull like dry fingers. Black bubbles rise in straight lines from below, ferry markers lean toward a half-submerged stone roof, and every sound seems to vanish before it reaches the open Mere.

locations.name: Drowned Bell-House
locations.description: A drowned stone bell-house tilts out of the Mere with its bronze belfry just above the waterline. The lower floor is half submerged, cold mineral water slaps the inner walls, and a great bell hangs inches above the black surface beside stairs leading down and an archive latch set high in the stone.

locations.name: Keeper's Air Pocket
locations.description: A brick service pocket beneath the bell deck holds one person's worth of stale air, Tamsin's hooded lantern, and a rusted pipe slick with condensation. A flooded lower stair opens through one side while an emergency shaft rises toward the bell deck overhead.

locations.name: Founders' Dry Archive
locations.description: A sealed stone archive above the old flood line smells of wax, dust, and mineral damp. Shelves hold wrapped ledgers and duty orders, while a relief map covers the back wall and a service-tunnel mark points toward Oakhaven's Founders' Crypt.

locations.name: Oakhaven ferry stair
locations.description: The ferry stair drops from Oakhaven's east street to a black skiff and a peg for a red scarf. The water here still has ripples. It smells of rope, tar, and cold iron. Noll Vey keeps the fare box nailed to the rail where he can see it without looking.

scenes.title: The Scarf Is Off the Peg
scenes.purpose: Hook the party at Oakhaven's ferry stair: Noll's apprentice is missing and a bell is ringing where the Mere should be quiet.
scenes.readAloud: Noll Vey stands on the ferry stair with one hand on the empty peg where Tamsin Reed's red scarf should be. The skiff knocks the piling in an ordinary way. Noll does not look ordinary. “She went to answer a bell,” he says. “The Mere is flat. Bells do not ring under flat water unless somebody built them to. I will pay you to bring her back. I will pay you more if you can tell me why the bell thinks it still has a job.”
gmNotes: Noll rows them. If he is refused or killed, the skiff is unlocked and Tamsin's chart is in the fare box. The night continues.
He believes the bell is a haunting. That belief is incomplete, not a lie he is telling on purpose.
Do not reveal the founders' diversion on the stair.

exitChoices.label: Cast off
exitChoices.description: Roll once before the chart is clear.

runSteps.title: Give the job
runSteps.text: Bring Tamsin back. Find out why the bell is ringing. Name the pay from the endings, not a new number.

runSteps.title: Show the empty peg
runSteps.text: The scarf is the personal stake. The bell is the mystery.

runSteps.title: Noll's limit
runSteps.text: He will not dive. He will row. If they attack him, use no stat block beyond a commoner and let the chart carry the job.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party is in the skiff or has taken it, and the stair is behind them.

scenes.title: A Bell Under Still Water
scenes.purpose: Establish Tamsin's disappearance, the underwater bell, and the idea that the haunting may be a warning rather than a predator.
scenes.readAloud: The Mere is flat enough to reflect the clouds without breaking them. Noll Vey's ferry sits tied at the landing, but Tamsin's red scarf is gone from its peg. Somewhere out beyond the reed islands, a bell rings once beneath the water. The sound reaches the dock through your boots before it reaches your ears.
gmNotes: Noll offers 100 gp total to recover Tamsin and explain the ringing.
Place three MERE LEVEL boxes on the table. Start at 0/3.
The party receives a flat-bottomed ferry, weighted line, and three cork floats.
Noll explicitly suggests the bell may be warning someone.

runSteps.title: State the rescue
runSteps.text: Tamsin vanished while checking the drowned bell-house.

runSteps.title: Show Mere Level
runSteps.text: Put three boxes on the table. Wrong bell sequences and long delays can raise the water.

runSteps.title: Frame the mystery
runSteps.text: Tell the party the ringing occurs only during blackwater seepage and still weather.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party pushes into the reed channel toward the drowned bell-house.

exitChoices.label: Cross the Silent Reeds
exitChoices.description: Follow Tamsin's ferry markers toward the submerged ruin.

scenes.title: The Silent Reeds
scenes.purpose: Deliver physical evidence that the Night Spring is flowing beneath the Mere and offer a mobile encounter that can be avoided.
scenes.readAloud: The channel narrows until reeds brush both sides of the ferry. Black bubbles rise in straight rows beneath you, each one popping without sound. Ahead, three white ferry markers lean toward the same sunken roof. Then something bumps the hull from below hard enough to rock the lantern.
gmNotes: Four Mere Skimmers circle the ferry but are attracted to vibration, not blood.
The party can distract them by throwing one cork float and striking the hull away from the bell-house; no check required.
A physical survey marker carved with NIGHT FLOW points directly from the Ashen Bridge direction toward the bell-house.
If combat occurs, skimmers retreat once one is bloodied.

runSteps.title: Show the current
runSteps.text: Describe the straight black bubble line and the physical NIGHT FLOW survey marker.

runSteps.title: Offer distraction
runSteps.text: The cork floats can pull skimmers away from the ferry without combat.

runSteps.title: Reach the roof
runSteps.text: The party arrives beside the tilted belfry and can tie off before entering.

scenes.advanceWhen: The ferry is secured to the drowned bell-house.

exitChoices.label: Enter the bell-house
exitChoices.description: Climb through the tilted belfry into the flooded ruin.

scenes.title: Low, High, Low
scenes.purpose: Present the sound puzzle, Ysra's warning behavior, and Tamsin's location before any player must commit to ringing the bell.
scenes.readAloud: The bronze bell hangs crooked above black water. One strike point near the rim is polished bright; another higher on the shoulder is green with age. Three carved water lines mark the wall: LOW WATER, ALARM, WITHDRAWN. A pale figure appears in the bell's reflection and raises one hand toward the carvings. Below the deck, someone knocks three times from behind a grate.
gmNotes: The intended sequence is LOW → HIGH → LOW.
Physical backup: the wall inscription shows low water, alarm above it, then water withdrawn back below.
Tamsin's charcoal rubbing in the grate repeats the same three symbols.
A wrong sequence raises Mere Level by 1 and triggers Grasping Water, but then Ysra points directly at the first correct strike point.
At Mere Level 3, the lower stair is fully submerged. Tamsin remains reachable through the emergency air shaft; the ending is never locked.
Completing LOW → HIGH → LOW opens the archive latch and makes Ysra non-hostile.

runSteps.title: Put two tones and three marks on the table
runSteps.text: LOW comes from the rim; HIGH comes from the shoulder; the wall shows LOW / ALARM / WITHDRAWN.

runSteps.title: Fail forward
runSteps.text: A wrong sequence raises the Mere, triggers the hazard, and causes Ysra to point at the first correct note.

runSteps.title: Open the archive
runSteps.text: The correct sequence releases the stone latch and stops Ysra's hostile water effects.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party has opened the archive latch and located Tamsin below.

exitChoices.label: Reach Tamsin
exitChoices.description: Use the lower stair or emergency air shaft to enter the keeper pocket.

scenes.title: Three Breaths of Air
scenes.purpose: Rescue Tamsin with fail-forward mechanics and preserve access even at maximum Mere Level.
scenes.readAloud: The keeper pocket is barely large enough for two people to crouch, and the trapped air tastes of rust and lamp smoke. Tamsin sits with her back against the brick, chin above the water, one hand wrapped around a pipe while the floodline trembles at her collar. She gives you a tired grin. “I had started to suspect Noll sent better swimmers.” Above her, the old emergency shaft knocks softly each time the Mere shifts.
gmNotes: At Mere Level 0–2, reach Tamsin through the lower stair: DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) to cross the flooded landing safely.
At Mere Level 3, use the emergency air shaft from the bell deck: DC 12 Athletics to lower/raise a rescuer with rope.
Failure never traps the party. On failure, take 1d6 bludgeoning from debris and reach Tamsin anyway.
Tamsin gives the party her charcoal rubbing and confirms HIGH → LOW was wrong.
Once freed, Tamsin can assist with one archive check or one final bell interaction, granting advantage.

runSteps.title: Choose the route
runSteps.text: Lower stair at Mere 0–2; emergency shaft at Mere 3.

runSteps.title: Resolve one crossing check
runSteps.text: Failure costs 1d6 bludgeoning but still reaches the air pocket.

runSteps.title: Bring Tamsin up
runSteps.text: Once rescued, she provides her rubbing and can assist one later check.

scenes.advanceWhen: Tamsin is out of the pocket and the archive can be entered.

exitChoices.label: Open the Founders' Archive
exitChoices.description: Read the records behind the bell latch.

scenes.title: The Founders Moved the Water
scenes.purpose: Reveal the series truth, give Ysra a release condition, and let players choose how to end the haunting.
scenes.readAloud: The archive is dry. Waxed ledgers fill stone shelves above an old flood line, and a relief map of Oakhaven covers the back wall. A black channel has been carved from beneath a building labeled FOUNDERS' CRYPT, across the east road, under the bridge, and into the Mere. On a hook below the map hangs Bellkeeper Ysra's final duty order: SOUND THE WARNING UNTIL ANSWERED.
gmNotes: The founder archive is the required truth source; Ysra's explanation is optional.
Players can RELEASE Ysra by reading the final duty order aloud and ringing LOW → HIGH → LOW one last time.
They can SILENCE the bell by removing the clapper after reading the archive; Ysra fades, but without closure.
They can PRESERVE the bell and leave Ysra bound after taking the records. This is legal but leaves the haunting active.
The relief map identifies a sealed service tunnel back toward Oakhaven's Founders' Crypt.
The town reward is highest if Tamsin survives and the archive is recovered, regardless of whether Ysra is released or silenced.

runSteps.title: Show the diversion
runSteps.text: Put the relief map in front of the table: Founders' Crypt → east road → Ashen Bridge → Mere.

runSteps.title: Make the final choice explicit
runSteps.text: Release Ysra, silence the bell after reading the truth, or preserve the warning and leave her bound.

runSteps.title: Carry the next lead
runSteps.text: The sealed service tunnel returns toward the Founders' Crypt for Module 07.

scenes.advanceWhen: The archive truth is recovered and the party chooses Ysra's fate.

exitChoices.label: Release Ysra
exitChoices.description: Repeat the answered warning and formally end her duty.

exitChoices.label: Silence the bell
exitChoices.description: Remove the clapper after recovering the archive truth.

exitChoices.label: Preserve the warning
exitChoices.description: Leave the bell and Ysra bound as an active warning station.

scenes.title: Resolution: Warning Answered
scenes.purpose: Close the mystery with Tamsin safe, Ysra released, and the founder diversion exposed.
scenes.readAloud: The final low note fades across the Mere instead of beneath it. Ysra appears once in the reflection beside Tamsin, no water pouring from her sleeves now. “Warning answered,” she says. Then the bell stops moving. At the landing, Noll grips Tamsin by both shoulders before remembering to pretend he is angry.
gmNotes: Award 125 gp total.

On the release ending, Noll gives Boots of Elvenkind (SRD 5.2, uncommon, no attunement line): silent steps and Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth). If your SRD 5.1 copy requires attunement, use that rule. The custom Boots of Elvenkind is not awarded.
The bell-house becomes quiet.
The Founders' Crypt service-tunnel map is retained for Module 07.

runSteps.title: Pay the rescue
runSteps.text: Award 125 gp total.

runSteps.title: Award closure
runSteps.text: Give the Boots of Elvenkind.

runSteps.title: Point home
runSteps.text: The archive route leads back beneath Oakhaven to the Founders' Crypt.

scenes.advanceWhen: Rewards and the Founders' Crypt map are recorded.

exitChoices.label: Return to Noll
exitChoices.description: Go back to Oakhaven and settle the job.

scenes.title: Resolution: A Quiet Mere
scenes.purpose: Honor a pragmatic ending that stops the haunting after the truth is preserved.
scenes.readAloud: When the clapper comes free, the bell rolls once in the current without making a sound. Ysra's reflection breaks into widening rings and does not return. Even the reeds outside seem louder afterward, and the ferry rope creaks against the landing in ordinary wind. The Mere is quiet again, but this time the silence feels chosen rather than waiting.
gmNotes: Award 110 gp total.
Tamsin survives and the archive truth is preserved.
No Boots of Elvenkind is awarded.
The service tunnel still points to the Founders' Crypt.

runSteps.title: Record pragmatic closure
runSteps.text: The bell cannot ring again; Ysra fades without formal release.

runSteps.title: Pay the work
runSteps.text: Award 110 gp total.

runSteps.title: Point home
runSteps.text: Carry the archive map toward the Founders' Crypt.

scenes.advanceWhen: The bell is silenced and the archive map is secured.

exitChoices.label: Return to Noll
exitChoices.description: Go back to Oakhaven and settle the job.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Bell Still Rings
scenes.purpose: Allow the party to preserve the active warning at the cost of leaving Ysra bound.
scenes.readAloud: The ferry noses back toward shore with the archive wrapped in oilcloth between your feet. Behind you, the drowned bell-house shrinks into gray water while reeds close over the channel. Just before the roof disappears, the bell rings once below the surface, the vibration traveling through the hull. Tamsin looks back. “At least now we know what it means.”
gmNotes: Award 100 gp total.
Ysra remains bound and the bell continues to sound during future contamination surges.
Noll accepts the choice if Tamsin is alive and the warning is understood.
The Founders' Crypt map remains the next lead.

runSteps.title: Record the continuing warning
runSteps.text: Ysra remains on duty and the bell continues functioning.

runSteps.title: Pay the investigation
runSteps.text: Award 100 gp total.

runSteps.title: Carry the truth
runSteps.text: The archive map points directly back to the Founders' Crypt.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party leaves with the archive and understands the ongoing bell warning.

exitChoices.label: Return to Noll
exitChoices.description: Go back to Oakhaven and settle the job.

scenes.title: Roll at the Stair
scenes.purpose: A rolled encounter at the ferry stair before the route across the Mere is clear.
scenes.readAloud: The stair's lower step is slick and the fare box ticks in the wash. Someone has tied a new cork float beside Noll's old one, painted like a channel buoy and pointing at open water that is not the bell-house. The skiff is ready. The direction is not, until you roll.
gmNotes: Roll 1d6 in the open. Use that row only. This is not a fixed fight.
The row never carries the only copy of a required clue. Skipping it does not stop the night.
1. A dock idler says the bell is a loose buoy knocking a hull. He has not been out. DC 10 Wisdom (Insight): he wants the ferry to stay shut so he can charge for rumors. The cork float is his.
2. DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) on the slick step. Failure: Prone, wet, no damage, and the fare box spills Tamsin's spare chalk.
3. A gull drops a scrap of reed-cloth with one stitched letter N. It matches the NIGHT FLOW marks later. It is not the only copy.

4. One SRD Hunter Shark fin in the stair's shadow. It leaves if they do not enter the water. 2014: Bite +6, reach 5 ft., 13 (2d8+4) piercing; Blood Frenzy; blindsight 30 ft. 2024: 14 (3d6+4), blindsight 60 ft. AC 12, HP 45, Water Breathing only. If they fight it here, remove one skimmer from the channel later.
5. Noll hums the wrong three notes on purpose, then stops, ashamed. Color. The real sequence is in the bell-house.
6. A coil of rope, 50 feet, mundane. Taking it helps the rescue and is not required.

exitChoices.label: Read the chart
exitChoices.description: The rolled row is done and the road continues.

runSteps.title: Roll in the open
runSteps.text: Tell the table this beat is a roll, not a scripted monster. Roll 1d6 where everyone can see it.

runSteps.title: Run only that row
runSteps.text: Read the matching row. If it is the combat row, offer the listed way out before initiative.

runSteps.title: Move on either way
runSteps.text: Success and failure both leave the party able to continue. Do not gate the next scene on this roll.

scenes.advanceWhen: One rolled row has been resolved and the party is moving again.

scenes.title: The Buoy Is Not the Bell
scenes.purpose: Give a clear course to the sunken bell-house and retire the loose-buoy red herring.
scenes.readAloud: Two courses are tied to the same piling. A new white cork float points at open water and a dock idler calls the bell a loose buoy knocking a hull. Tamsin's chart, still folded in the fare box, draws a line of soundings from the Ashen Bridge's direction to a square marked BELL, and that square is not where the white float points. Noll has orange paint under one nail and none of the white. He looks at the float as if it owes him money. He does not say he is sure.
gmNotes: Quest giver is Noll Vey, the ferryman. He wants Tamsin Reed back and he will pay to know why the bell is ringing. He believes it is a haunting. That belief is incomplete. The mayor does not give this job.

Lead A, red herring: the white buoy and the idler. Motive: the idler wants the ferry shut so he can charge for rumors. The paint is fresh and the wrong color. Tamsin paints buoys orange. Chasing the float costs about ten minutes and finds empty water.
Lead B: Noll. Motive: fear for his apprentice, and a habit of blaming ghosts before paper. He will row. He will not dive. If he is refused or dead, the chart is still in the fare box.
Lead C, physical: Tamsin's chart and, if they found it, the reed-cloth scrap stitched with N. The chart is the course. It does not explain the founders yet.
Let them question the idler and Noll, and let them row the wrong water once. The square on the chart is still there when they come back.

runSteps.title: Put the leads on the table
runSteps.text: Name the people and the physical claims. Let the players choose the order. Do not announce which one is true.

runSteps.title: Play the motive
runSteps.text: Each person wants something. A false lead has a reason. Answer questions in that person's voice.

runSteps.title: Wrong turns fail forward
runSteps.text: Checking the red herring costs about ten minutes. The true route is still in their hands afterward, on paper or on the ground.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party is rowing the chart's line, not the decoy.

scenes.title: Roll on the Crossing
scenes.purpose: A rolled encounter while traveling the Mere toward the bell-house.
scenes.readAloud: The Mere goes flat as soon as the stair is behind you. Ripples die without a reason you can point at. Reed islands stand like stitches. Somewhere ahead a bell rings once, under the water, and the skiff's boards answer it through your boots. You are not at the landing. Roll.
gmNotes: Roll 1d6 in the open. Use that row only. This is not a fixed fight.
The row never carries the only copy of a required clue. Skipping it does not stop the night.
1. A floating oar, Tamsin's initials burned in the grip. DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) spots it. Failure: it knocks the hull and they have it anyway.
2. DC 10 Strength (Athletics) against a reed snag. Failure: lose five minutes cutting free. The bell rings again so they cannot miss the direction.
3. Fog for one minute. It hides nothing that matters. The chart still points.
4. A single Mere Skimmer bumps the hull and leaves. Use the Hunter Shark block if they attack. Otherwise it is a warning, not initiative.
5. Noll, if present, almost says the founders' names and swallows them. He does not know the diversion. Do not give it away.
6. A dry tin with chalk and a half-rubbing of one bell note. It helps the puzzle later and is not the only rubbing.

exitChoices.label: Reach the landing
exitChoices.description: The rolled row is done and the road continues.

runSteps.title: Roll in the open
runSteps.text: Tell the table this beat is a roll, not a scripted monster. Roll 1d6 where everyone can see it.

runSteps.title: Run only that row
runSteps.text: Read the matching row. If it is the combat row, offer the listed way out before initiative.

runSteps.title: Move on either way
runSteps.text: Success and failure both leave the party able to continue. Do not gate the next scene on this roll.

scenes.advanceWhen: One rolled row has been resolved and the party is moving again.

scenes.title: Noll Takes the Count
scenes.purpose: Return to Oakhaven's ferry stair and settle with Noll, including the Boots of Elvenkind if Ysra was released.
scenes.readAloud: The ferry stair has ripples again, or it does not, and Oakhaven can hear the difference from the street. Noll is at the peg. He does not ask about founders first. He asks whether Tamsin climbed the stair under her own power. The fare box is open. Inside it, under the coin, is a pair of soft grey boots that do not quite touch the wood the way boots should.
gmNotes: Pay the gold from the ending they chose.

Release ending: the boots are Boots of Elvenkind. No attunement in either edition. 2014: steps make no sound, and advantage only on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that rely on moving silently. 2024: steps make no sound regardless of the surface, and Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Silence and Preserve endings do not include the boots. The custom Boots of Elvenkind is retired. Series level-6 pregens assume the release ending.

runSteps.title: Tamsin first
runSteps.text: Say whether she is alive. Noll's face follows that answer, not the politics.

runSteps.title: Pay and boots
runSteps.text: Coin always. Boots only if Ysra was released.

runSteps.title: What the town will say
runSteps.text: Ask what they tell Oakhaven about the founders. That choice is already in the ending.

scenes.advanceWhen: Noll has paid, Tamsin's fate is known, and any boots have been given or withheld.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Stair under the Town
scenes.purpose: End the Mere and point at the Founders' Crypt, which is the planned level-7 module and is not written yet.
scenes.readAloud: The service-tunnel sketch from the archive, or Noll's copy of the rubbing, ends under a building the town still uses. The label is plain: FOUNDERS' CRYPT. The passage is sealed on the Oakhaven side by a door the ferry stair does not open. Noll folds the paper. “That is not a bell,” he says. “That is the people who moved the water. I will not row you there. It is under our own street, and it can wait until you are ready to knock.”
gmNotes: Level 7, the Founders' Crypt, is planned and not written. Do not improvise it as a published module. Stop on the lead.
This module was worth the step from 6 toward 7. Say that, then stop.
The archive map, Ysra's memory, and this rubbing are three sources. Losing Noll does not erase the paper.

runSteps.title: Show the crypt
runSteps.text: The passage returns under Oakhaven to the Founders' Crypt.

runSteps.title: Say it is not ready
runSteps.text: The next module is not on the table yet. Do not invent the crypt's rooms.

runSteps.title: Close
runSteps.text: End at the stair.

scenes.advanceWhen: The crypt lead is recorded and play stops.

clues.revelation: Ysra is repeating an old contamination warning rather than trying to drown intruders.
sources: A physical NIGHT FLOW survey marker points from the blackwater channel toward the bell-house.
The bell-house wall inscription labels the ringing pattern CONTAMINATION WARNING.
Ysra points at the warning inscription and water marks instead of attacking Tamsin.

clues.revelation: The warning sequence is LOW → HIGH → LOW.
sources: The physical wall inscription shows LOW WATER, ALARM, then WITHDRAWN beneath three strike symbols.
Tamsin's charcoal rubbing records the same three water-line marks.
Bellkeeper Ysra's ritual phrase is 'Water below. Alarm above. Water withdrawn.'

clues.revelation: Tamsin is alive in the keeper's trapped air pocket.
sources: Three knocks come through the physical service grate below the bell deck.
Tamsin's lit hooded lantern is visible through bubbles under the lower stair.
A fresh rope track leads from the bell deck toward the emergency air shaft.

clues.revelation: Oakhaven's founders deliberately diverted the Night Spring away from their crypt and toward the Mere.
sources: The physical relief map in the dry archive shows the diversion carved from the Founders' Crypt to the Mere.
A waxed founder record orders the spring channel moved east before crypt construction.
Ysra's sealed duty order references contamination 'from the founder diversion line.'

clues.revelation: A sealed service tunnel returns from the bell-house system toward the Founders' Crypt beneath Oakhaven.
sources: The archive relief map labels a maintenance tunnel CRYPT RELIEF.
A physical brass key tag in the archive reads FOUNDERS' SERVICE TUNNEL.
Ysra remembers maintenance crews coming from Oakhaven through the same dry passage.

encounters.name: Mere Skimmers
encounters.difficulty: below Low (1800 XP; Low 2400 for four level-6 characters)
encounters.summary: Two vibration-hunting aquatic scavengers bump and climb the ferry on the approach to the bell-house.
encounters.objective: Reach the drowned bell-house without losing the ferry.
encounters.resolution: Distract, drive off, or bloody the skimmers; they do not pursue into the ruin.
encounters.talkOut: They are animals and do not negotiate.
encounters.bypass: Throw a cork float and strike the water away from the bell-house; the skimmers follow it for long enough to reach the ruin.

encounters.name: Bellkeeper Ysra's Warning
encounters.summary: Ysra creates pushing water when the party mishandles the bell but becomes non-hostile after the correct warning sequence.
encounters.objective: Understand and answer the warning without destroying the bell.
encounters.resolution: Ring LOW → HIGH → LOW, or survive long enough to interpret the physical inscriptions and repeat the sequence.
encounters.talkOut: Present the warning inscription, keeper badge, or two correct notes; Ysra responds with ritual phrases and gestures.
encounters.bypass: The archive latch can also be forced with DC 15 Athletics after the truth is understood, but the bell sequence still releases Ysra cleanly.
encounters.special: Wrong sequences raise Mere Level but reveal more of the correct answer.

encounters.name: The Bellkeeper's Release
encounters.summary: After the archive opens, the party decides whether to release Ysra, silence the bell, or preserve the ongoing warning.
encounters.objective: Choose Ysra's fate after the founder diversion truth is recovered.
encounters.resolution: Read the duty order and ring the answered warning, remove the clapper, or leave the warning intact.
encounters.talkOut: Ysra accepts release, resists premature destruction, and remains bound if the party preserves the bell.
encounters.bypass: No combat is required. If Ysra was made hostile, the physical archive still enables all three endings.
encounters.special: The choice changes reward and future bell-house state, not access to Module 07.

puzzles.name: Water Below, Alarm Above
puzzles.prompt: The bell has LOW and HIGH strike points. Three carved water-line symbols read LOW WATER, ALARM, WITHDRAWN.
puzzles.failForward: A wrong sequence raises Mere Level by 1 and triggers Grasping Water, but Ysra then points directly to the first correct LOW strike point.

traps.name: Grasping Water
traps.trigger: Ring an incorrect three-note bell sequence.
traps.effect: Creatures on the bell deck make DC 12 Strength saves; on a failure they are pulled 5 ft. toward the flooded edge and take 1d6 cold damage.
traps.failForward: Mere Level rises by 1, but Ysra reveals the first correct LOW note and the puzzle remains fully solvable.

items.effect: Provides a physical LOW / ALARM / WITHDRAWN clue.

items.name: Boots of Elvenkind
items.description: Soft grey boots from the fare box, given if Ysra is released.
items.effect: No attunement in either edition. 2014: steps make no sound, and advantage only on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that rely on moving silently. 2024: steps make no sound regardless of the surface, and Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. The custom Mereglass Token is not awarded.

items.name: Founder Diversion Map
items.description: A waxed relief map showing the Night Spring redirected from the Founders' Crypt to the Mere.

endings.name: Warning Answered
endings.condition: Archive recovered and Ysra formally released with the answered warning.
endings.result: Tamsin safe; 125 gp; Boots of Elvenkind; bell quiet; Founders' Crypt lead.

endings.name: A Quiet Mere
endings.condition: Archive recovered and bell clapper removed.
endings.result: Tamsin safe; 110 gp; bell silent; Ysra fades without formal release; Founders' Crypt lead.

endings.name: The Bell Still Rings
endings.condition: Archive recovered and warning bell left active.
endings.result: Tamsin safe; 100 gp; Ysra remains bound as warning keeper; Founders' Crypt lead.

policies: Every wrong bell attempt reveals more of the correct answer; the sound puzzle cannot dead-end.
Maximum flooding changes the rescue route but never locks the ending.
If an NPC is absent or hostile, physical inscriptions and archive records preserve every required truth.

routes.trigger: Noll is refused, missing, unavailable, or dead before the party launches.
routes.response: Tamsin's empty ferry, red scarf, weighted line, and route markers remain at the landing. A physical note on the ferry says she went to the drowned bell-house.
stateChanges: The ferry and approach tools remain available.

routes.trigger: The party attacks Ysra, makes her hostile, or tries to destroy the bell before she can explain the warning.
routes.response: The physical warning inscription, Tamsin's rubbing, and archive mechanism still reveal LOW → HIGH → LOW. Ysra defends the bell with pushing water but never removes clues.
stateChanges: The three finale choices remain available after the archive opens.

routes.trigger: The party skips or bypasses the main bell deck using swimming, magic, or the emergency shaft.
routes.response: They can still rescue Tamsin and reach the archive latch from below. Tamsin's rubbing and the archive inscription provide the sequence when they return to the bell.
stateChanges: The puzzle can be solved from either direction.

routes.trigger: The party leaves the ruin after locating Tamsin but before resolving the bell.
routes.response: Increase Mere Level by one when they return, maximum 3. Tamsin's air pocket and the emergency shaft remain safe enough for the one-shot.

pathPressure.principle: Careful investigation makes the bell sequence and rescue safer, but rushing never locks the ending; the party can still finish at Mere Level 3 through the emergency shaft and physical archive clues.
prepared: Using the cork float bypasses the Mere Skimmers without spending combat resources.
Reading the wall inscription before ringing prevents unnecessary Mere Level increases.
rushed: Wrong bell sequences raise the Mere and add Grasping Water hazards.
Skipping the normal lower stair forces the party to use the tighter emergency shaft at Mere Level 3.

cutOrder: If the table is behind, resolve each rolled row in one sentence. Do not skip the return to Oakhaven or the lead into the next module.
If 20+ minutes behind, remove the Mere Skimmers and deliver the NIGHT FLOW marker as the ferry reaches the ruin.
If 15+ minutes behind at the bell, have Tamsin's rubbing already visible through the grate.
Never cut Tamsin's rescue, the founder diversion reveal, or Ysra's final choice.
optionalOrder: Combat with Mere Skimmers instead of float distraction.
Additional founder-record reading after the service tunnel is identified.

encounters.bypass: Throw one cork float and strike the water away from the ruin. The skimmers follow it. They breathe only underwater and cannot chase across the deck.

creatures.name: Mere Skimmer
creatures.speed: 2014: 0 ft., swim 40 ft. 2024: 5 ft., swim 40 ft.
creatures.statBlock: SRD Hunter Shark, reskinned as a Mere skimmer. Large. Water Breathing only. AC 12, HP 45, CR 2, 450 XP.
creatures.attack: 2014: Bite +6, reach 5 ft., 13 (2d8+4) piercing; Blood Frenzy; blindsight 30 ft. 2024: 14 (3d6+4), blindsight 60 ft. Bite +6, reach 5 ft., Advantage if the target is missing any Hit Points.
creatures.trait: Water Breathing: it can breathe only underwater. It can reach a creature at the rail and cannot chase across the deck. A struck cork float within 60 feet draws the skimmers for 1 round.
creatures.edition2024: 2024: 14 (3d6+4), blindsight 60 ft. Bite +6, reach 5 ft., Advantage if the target is missing any Hit Points. AC 12, HP 45.
creatures.tactics: Ram the hull, bite anyone in the water or leaning on the rail, and break off when bloodied. They are not the mystery.

encounters.end: Skimmers are distracted, driven away, or one is bloodied.
encounters.balance: SRD 5.2.1 for 4 level-6 characters: Low 2400, Moderate 4000, High 5600. Creature XP spent: 1800, below the Low budget. Four hunter sharks stay under Low for four level-6 characters. They cannot cross the deck. The bell is the point. encounters.balanceWhy: Four hunter sharks stay under Low for four level-6 characters. They cannot cross the deck. The bell is the point.

rulesEditions.carryForward: Level 6 sheets add the Boots of Elvenkind on Ness Quinn and still carry the wand, cloak, pearl, and +1 longsword.
rulesEditions.unsettled: Settled against SRD 5.1 and SRD 5.2.1. No 2014 Easy/Medium/Hard/Deadly labels, because SRD 5.1 has no encounter-budget table. Boots of Elvenkind need no attunement in either edition; 2014 advantage is only on Stealth checks that rely on moving silently. Wand of Secrets: 2014 an action within 30 feet; 2024 a Magic action within 60 feet. 2014 Life always prepares Spiritual Weapon from level 3 and Beacon of Hope from level 5. 2024 Life does not. Hunter Shark and Giant Constrictor Snake are printed in both edition blocks.
